title: Parametric Lease-Up Delay Insurance
one_liner: Insurance that pays automatically if a public submarket days-to-lease index stays high during a building's lease-up, protecting developers' interest carry.
customer: Multifamily developers and construction and mezzanine lenders with 100-400 unit buildings in lease-up (1.2M units nationally), sold through debt brokers.
problem: Lease-up interest carry balloons when time-to-lease stretches (34 days, longest September since 2019, with concessions on 15.8% of stabilized units). Lenders demand reserves or personal guarantees, sponsors self-insure, and traditional delay-in-start-up cover only addresses physical damage.
solution: A parametric policy that pays a pre-agreed sum if an index of median days-to-lease or vacancy exceeds a strike for N months in the lease-up window. Priced with an actuarial model, backed by reinsurer capacity, and sold as carry cover or a lender-accepted replacement for personal guarantees.
why_now: Lease-up glut and tight balance sheets create demand, parametric infrastructure (fronting carriers, index data, automated payouts) has matured, and starts are down 15.5%, so risk may be front-loaded.
revenue_model: 6-10% rate on line on $1-5M limits, plus MGA commission and profit share.
non_obvious_insight: Developers cannot influence a submarket's days-to-lease, so it is transparent and free of fraud, which makes it insurable. Capacity providers can view this as a defined macro bet with a supply-starts-driven mean reversion, though correlation across deals is the key risk.
first_30_days: Build an index from public rent and vacancy data. Quote 10 hypothetical developer and lender deals. Partner with a parametric MGA or coverholder for risk-carrying capacity and sign one $500K-limit pilot.

title: Mod-Neutral Escrow for Reddit Swap Subs
one_liner: A roughly 2% escrow-and-reputation rail for r/hardwareswap-style trade communities that auto-writes verified trade counts, so buyers stop gambling on PayPal Goods & Services and mods stop refereeing scams.
customer: Buyers and sellers of $300-$5,000 used goods in Reddit trade subs (GPUs/RAM/SSDs, mechanical keyboards, watches, cameras, audio gear). Fee is split between both sides. Power traders and flippers are the first users because they feel chargeback pain most.
problem: Reddit's swap subs are unofficial high-ticket marketplaces run on mod-maintained 'confirmed trades' flair and PayPal G&S. Sellers get hit by chargebacks or 'not as described' reversals weeks later, even with signature confirmation. Buyers get hit by bogus-escrow scams and friends-and-family requests. Leaving for eBay costs about 13%, and PayPal G&S costs about 3.5% plus a fixed fee. Mods burn hours every week adjudicating disputes with no tooling. They also cannot endorse a paid vendor, because the Moderator Code of Conduct (Rule 5) bars compensation for moderation actions.
solution: Buyer funds are held through a licensed escrow partner. The seller ships with tracking, signature, and a serial-number photo checklist. Funds release after delivery plus a 72-hour inspection window. Disputes go to an evidence packet reviewed by a small paid panel of trusted high-volume traders. Every completed trade writes to a public read-only 'verified trades' API, plus a free Devvit flair-sync app any mod team can install to update trade counts automatically. Mods are never paid and the rail never touches moderation decisions.
why_now: The 2024-present global memory shortage has pushed RAM, SSD and GPU prices up several-fold, and a June 2026 class action alleges DRAM price fixing. That makes used-parts ticket sizes large enough that a 2% escrow fee is cheap insurance. Chargeback fraud on P2P payments is also a growing complaint among sellers.
revenue_model: 1.5-2.5% fee per side (undercutting PayPal G&S and eBay), optional insured-shipping add-on, and later a partner revenue share or float income on held funds. Enterprise-style deals with high-volume resellers who trade weekly.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is mod-trusted neutrality, not payments tech. Mods can't take money and won't bless a vendor who could be partial, so the winning rail is the one that is publicly documented, has zero mod financial relationship, and hands mods a free tool that deletes their number-one time sink (dispute refereeing and manual flair updates). Adoption is pulled by mod teams, not pushed by marketing. Serious traders also fear the 60-180 day chargeback tail more than the fee.
first_30_days: Sign with a licensed escrow or payments partner (an Escrow.com-style API, or Stripe Connect with held funds) so you avoid money-transmitter licensing. Start in one tight, high-ticket niche such as watches or keyboards rather than r/hardwareswap itself. Recruit 15 top-flair traders as design partners and waive fees on their first 30 trades. Build the Devvit flair-sync app and a public transparency page. Target about 200 escrowed trades at about $600 average, and track dispute rate and time-to-release as the proof points for mod teams.

title: Trust-Fund Compliance for Family Vloggers
one_liner: A minutes-on-screen tracker and escrow tool that computes, sets aside and documents the trust share owed to kids who appear in monetized family channels.
customer: Family channel operators on YouTube, TikTok and Instagram earning $50k+ a year, influencer agencies and MCNs, and brands and payment processors that want a 'clean hands' certificate.
problem: Several states have passed laws on minors in monetized content: Illinois (2024) requires a trust share by on-screen time, Minnesota (2025) restricts under-14 content creation for pay, and California extended Coogan-style protections (details from memory). Parents compute set-asides by hand. Brands and platforms are exposed, and grown kids and documentaries are fueling backlash.
solution: The tool ingests channel data, uses vision models to measure each child's on-screen minutes per video, computes the state-specific set-aside, generates records and moves funds into a custodial trust, UTMA or custodial investment account. It also keeps consent and deletion logs and issues brand-facing compliance certificates.
why_now: The state laws took effect in 2024-25, public scrutiny of family-vlogging is at a high, and a new custodial-account channel (Trump Accounts, opened July 2026, per the brief) gives set-asides a natural home.
revenue_model: $99-499 a month per channel or about 1% of earnings, plus per-campaign brand compliance certificates.
non_obvious_insight: The real buyers are brands and platforms that need a clean-hands certificate, and creators who need to avoid legal exposure. It works like marketplace sales-tax automation, and the child is the beneficiary, not the customer.
first_30_days: Ship a free on-screen-minutes calculator. DM 100 family channels with 50k-2M subscribers. Sell a $299 compliance setup with an attorney-reviewed template. Approach 3 influencer agencies for a group deal.

title: Quality-of-Earnings Audits for Robot Fleets
one_liner: A finance-native auditor that verifies deployed units, productive hours, teleoperation share and revenue per robot for the lenders, lessors and investors underwriting robot, AV and drone fleets.
customer: Lenders, equipment lessors, SPAC sponsors, growth funds and acquirers underwriting robotics, AV and drone companies. Second wave: insurers of AV trucks and warehouse robots, and investors in robot-as-a-service lease pools.
problem: Robotics valuations run on self-reported fleet metrics. Agility reported $1.8M of 2025 revenue against a $2.5B SPAC. Maven raised $100M with about 8 robots deployed. Serve booked about $1.3k of revenue per robot. Figure reports about 740 robots against about 600 employees. 1X NEO's early demos were largely teleoperated. Nobody audits 'deployed' vs 'productive' vs 'autonomous' vs 'paid'. AV insurers price 'slightly above' human trucks on the unknown, and lessors cannot underwrite $499-$600/mo robot leases blind.
solution: A boutique assurance firm. Under NDA it gets read-only telemetry, remote-assist logs and billing, and visits sites. It produces a signed Fleet QoE report with standard metrics: units deployed vs productive hours, human interventions per robot-hour, revenue and margin per unit, safety events, uptime and maintenance cost, and contract quality. Later, publish a standard 'Fleet Passport' for covenant reporting.
why_now: About 22,000 humanoids shipped in H1 2026. Unitree IPO'd in Aug 2026. Agility is going public via SPAC. Figure plans a $600/mo lease. Skild ($14B) and Physical Intelligence ($11B) are priced for perfection. Leasing and asset-backed structures for robots are being invented now, and capital allocators need evidence, not demos.
revenue_model: $40k-$120k per diligence engagement, buyer-paid. $10k-$30k per year of continuous covenant monitoring for lenders and lessors. An anonymized benchmark data license to insurers.
non_obvious_insight: The metric that decides whether a robotics company is a software business or a labor-arbitrage business, hidden human-intervention hours per robot-hour, is invisible to the buyer. Capital allocators, not vendors, must be the payer, because vendor-paid attestation fails (Trustpilot was fined for selling to those it rates). An ex-assurance plus ex-robotics team beats a technical certifier.
first_30_days: Write a 40-item data request and an intervention-hour analysis template. Recruit an ex-Big-4 assurance lead and one robotics ops engineer. Offer two free pilot audits to a debt fund or equipment lessor with a robot deal in progress. Publish an anonymized 'what to ask a robotics CEO' metrics guide. Aim for one paid engagement letter within 60-90 days.

title: Paid Shelter-Dog Field Trips, Fees Per Adoption
one_liner: Professional walkers take the longest-stay shelter dogs on 3-hour public field trips with photos and behavior reports, and shelters pay a small trip fee plus a success fee for each adoption.
customer: Municipal and county shelters and large humane societies (paying for outcomes), with pet-food brands, pet insurers, and community foundations as sponsors.
problem: Big adult dogs, especially bully-breed types, sit in kennels for months. Kennel stress makes them look their worst: barking, spinning, lunging. Adopters decide in about 30 seconds. Volunteers do field trips but are untrained for the hard dogs, unreliable, and unscalable. Every extra day in the kennel costs the shelter real money and raises the odds of a bad outcome.
solution: A walker collects the dog for a 3-hour outing in an 'Adopt Me' vest along a cafe, park, and errand route. They shoot 10 standardized photos and video, and file a behavior report (leash manners, other dogs, cats, car ride, house-training, energy). That content goes onto the shelter's listing and a hyperlocal 'Dog of the Week' list pushed through the walker's client network. Adopted dogs get a paid 7-day decompression check-in that also reduces returns. Everything is tracked against matched dogs to prove the effect on length of stay.
why_now: Shelters have been running over capacity for the past few years, with intake outpacing adoption and large dogs backing up, and budgets are tight. Housing and landlord pet restrictions keep driving relinquishments. Funders and municipalities increasingly want outcome-based spending, and walkers now have the cheap phone video and social distribution to make a dog look like a dog and not like a kennel number. I could not re-verify current national shelter statistics in this session, so quote local data in the pitch.
revenue_model: About $35 to $50 per field trip paid by the shelter or a sponsor, plus a $150 to $300 success fee per adoption within 30 days. Benchmark the success fee against the shelter's own cost per kennel day. Optional sponsored 'field trip' slots from pet brands and insurers, and grant funding to seed the first shelter.
non_obvious_insight: A dog is evaluated in the worst possible environment, and the fix is not better marketing, it is moving the evaluation out of the kennel. Professional walkers have exactly what volunteers lack: leash skill with hard dogs, idle midday capacity, and a trusted network of 50 to 100 households that will actually meet a dog because the walker they trust is holding the leash.
first_30_days: Offer the shelter's volunteer or foster coordinator a free pilot on the 10 longest-stay dogs, with two or three of your own walkers. Track days-to-adoption against similar dogs not taken out. After 30 days, hand the director a one-page results sheet and ask for a paid pilot, or apply for a local pet-industry or community foundation grant to fund the first 100 trips.

title: Peak-Window Uptime Plans for Fishing Boats
one_liner: A seasonal membership that pre-stages each boat's likely failure parts and rebuilt swap components in the harbor, provides RSW and hydraulic mechanics on call, and later adds a paid lost-peak-days cover.
customer: Bristol Bay and Prince William Sound drift and set net owners, plus seiners, who pay $2,000-4,000 per boat per season. A fleet of a few hundred boats is a $1M-plus business. Later an insurance partner underwrites the lost-time cover.
problem: Most of a boat's year is earned in about 10-14 days. With 2026's $1.72/lb, a busy boat can earn $5-15K a day at peak. Hull and machinery insurance pays for repair, never for the lost fishing days. A raw-water impeller, hydraulic hose, reel motor, fuel filter or failed RSW system takes a boat out for three days because the part is on a barge or a bush flight that's booked solid. The whole fleet breaks the same dozen components in the same ten days.
solution: Catalog the top 15-20 failure modes by engine and hydraulic setup. Stage member-funded kits in secure containers at Naknek, Dillingham, Egegik and similar harbors by June 1. Hold a rotating pool of rebuilt swap cores (injection pumps, hydraulic pumps, reel motors). Contract freelance diesel, hydraulic and RSW mechanics on retainer for guaranteed response times. Members can order from the grounds by satellite text. Phase two: verified downtime (AIS, dock check-in, mechanic log) triggers a fixed per-day payment during declared peak windows through an MGA partner.
why_now: The 2026 price rebound made every fishing day worth much more than in 2025. The fleet is aging. RSW is now paid for (about $0.15/lb bonus at some processors), yet the regional development association is funding apprentices because there aren't enough RSW technicians. Starlink lets skippers order parts and report faults from the fishing grounds.
revenue_model: Membership fees of $2-4K per boat per season, parts and swap-core margin, mechanic call-out fees, and a later per-day parametric lost-time premium shared with the underwriter.
non_obvious_insight: Downtime costs are about timing, not repair. The scarce resource at peak is the right part on the right beach within hours, and nobody sells that. It works as pooled inventory: because the fleet fails predictably, a small stockpile insures hundreds of boats. Insurance pooling for parts is cheaper and faster to launch than insurance pooling for money.
first_30_days: Interview 30 skippers and mechanics at the November Pacific Marine Expo in Seattle and by phone with Naknek and Dillingham crews. Build the failure-mode parts list by engine and hydraulic setup. Pre-sell 40 memberships with $500 deposits by February. Line up two freelance mechanics and one RSW tech. Rent a container in one harbor and stage the first 40 boats' kits by June 1.

title: Front Door for AI Callers at Local Businesses
one_liner: A phone-number layer that recognizes when the caller is an AI agent, answers instantly with pre-authorized quotes and availability, and routes real customers to humans.
customer: Owner-operated local service businesses (salons, groomers, HVAC and plumbing, auto shops, cleaners) with 1-20 staff, reached via marketing agencies and booking or field-service platforms. AI receptionist vendors are later licensees.
problem: Google's 'Have AI check pricing' agentic calling has rolled out to US Search users and expanded to home services in summer 2026. Businesses now get AI callers that tie up staff and harvest prices, and owners cannot tell agents from customers. In Microsoft's Magentic Marketplace simulation, buyer agents heavily favored the first proposal they received, so fast structured answers win business.
solution: Answer with an agent detector and an agent lane. If the caller identifies as or behaves like an AI (or presents a signed handshake), reply with a spoken and machine-readable quote from the owner's rate card and calendar within owner-set bounds, and log the outcome. Real customers go to humans. Publish a URL or DTMF handshake so compliant agents can switch from speech to structured data, the Gibberlink idea done with production-grade channels. Analytics show which agents call and quote win rates.
why_now: Agentic calling is live at Google scale, AI receptionists are common, and the 2025 Gibberlink demo proved the handshake idea but remains a proof of concept. Production agent protocols (MCP, A2A) do not cover phone calls to small businesses.
revenue_model: $49-$149/month per location, agency white-label deals, and later per-verified-handshake fees from agent platforms.
non_obvious_insight: The phone is the API of the local economy and both ends are becoming machines that still talk in speech. Whoever owns the switch-to-data handshake and the seller's rate-card truth owns local agent commerce, and speed to first quote may matter more than price.
first_30_days: Build the call flow on a telephony API. Recruit 20 salons, groomers and HVAC shops through 3 local marketing agencies, log the AI calls they receive (many owners are unaware), and show AI calls answered and quotes won. Charge $79/month.

title: Digital Legacy Setup Sold Through Wealth Advisors
one_liner: A white-labeled 'digital safety and legacy' visit for advisors' 80+ clients, paid for by the advisor as a retention and heir-acquisition tool.
customer: Independent RIAs and trust departments with $100M-$2B in assets and many clients over 78, plus elder-law attorneys as a secondary channel.
problem: Industry surveys often find that a majority of heirs fire their parents' advisor after an inheritance. Regulators also expect vigilance on senior clients, with trusted-contact requirements (FINRA 4512) and hold authority (Rule 2165). Meanwhile the 80-year-old's digital life (email, photos, passwords, crypto, cloud accounts, carrier, bank portals) is unmanaged. When they die or lose capacity the family can't get in, and scammers can.
solution: A 90-minute in-home or video visit by a trained 'digital steward': account inventory, password manager and passkey setup, Apple Legacy Contact and Google Inactive Account Manager set up, carrier port-out locks and credit freezes, bank alerts with 2FA routed to a trusted contact, and a family emergency binder handed to the heir or trustee. The heir joins the final visit, introduced by the advisor as the person who organized it. Add an annual re-check.
why_now: The multi-trillion-dollar generational wealth transfer is underway. More wealth sits in crypto and online accounts. Deepfake voice-clone scams target seniors. Apple and Google have shipped legacy-contact features but adoption is low, and FINRA's 2026 oversight report keeps trusted-contact practices in focus.
revenue_model: $450-900 per client visit paid by the advisor, who may pass it through, plus a $150/yr maintenance subscription. Referral fees from elder-law attorneys.
non_obvious_insight: The payer isn't the 80-year-old. It's the advisor, whose most valuable asset, the client relationship, is about to leave with the heirs. A digital steward visit is a useful favor that puts the advisor in the room with the next generation, and it doubles as compliance-friendly protection.
first_30_days: Recruit 5-10 RIAs through one advisor community (XYPN or local FPA chapters) and offer 3 free client visits each in exchange for feedback and a signed pilot. Hire retired IT pros or college students and train them on a checklist. Track how many heirs attend and whether advisors get follow-up meetings.

title: Dog Walk Plus: Wellness Checks for Isolated Seniors
one_liner: Turn the daily dog walk at an older client's home into a consented, structured wellness check with escalation, sold to their adult children.
customer: Adult children of independent-living parents who own dogs and live alone (the payer). Later: geriatric care managers, home health agencies, senior housing operators, and long-term care insurers.
problem: A dog walker is the only outsider who enters an older person's home every day at a predictable hour. I have found clients on the floor, and noticed early cognitive decline: the dog fed twice or not at all, pills left out, mail piling up, new bruises. Adult children call and ask us informally, we have no protocol, no consent, and no escalation ladder. Seniors refuse pendants and sensors but accept a walker, because it is about the dog and their dignity stays intact. The dog is also why many seniors delay going to the ER.
solution: A 'Walk Plus' plan built on a written consent from the senior. Alongside the walk, the walker does a 60-second structured check (a 10-tap list covering mobility, orientation, medications visible, food in the fridge, home temperature, bruises, mood, dog condition). Family gets a weekly text summary with trend flags. There is a clear escalation ladder (no answer at the door, then family call, then agreed non-emergency welfare check), and a pet emergency plan with keys and authority on file so that if the owner is hospitalized the walker becomes the dog's custodian. That prevents surrenders and removes the reason to refuse the hospital.
why_now: A large cohort is turning 65 and aging in place, home-care aide capacity is tight, and adult children are stretched thin as remote caregivers. Structured notes are now easy to summarize into a plain-language weekly update. Health plans and senior-service providers are looking for cheap ways to catch problems early, and a daily reason to enter the home is exactly what monitoring products lack.
revenue_model: Walks at $25 to $45 per visit plus a $29 to $49 monthly check-in fee paid by the family. B2B later: license the protocol and reporting to home health agencies and senior housing operators, and sell trend data (with consent) to long-term care insurers or aging-in-place programs.
non_obvious_insight: The dog is the Trojan horse that makes monitoring acceptable. A pendant says 'you're frail'; a dog walker says 'I'm here for the dog.' Walkers already do this informally and unpaid, so the product is less a new service than a protocol, a consent form, and an escalation path around something that already happens every day.
first_30_days: Convert existing senior clients (most walkers have three to six) with a one-page consent form. Build the check-in with a form and Twilio text summaries, no app needed. Partner with two local geriatric care managers who charge by the hour for the same visibility, and post in senior center and church newsletters. Target 10 paying families and track escalations as your proof.

title: Pay-Per-Attendance Social Prescriptions for Loneliness
one_liner: A settlement layer where health systems and employers pay small local groups (Men's Sheds, choirs, walking clubs) a fixed fee for every verified attendance by a doctor-referred lonely patient.
customer: Nonprofit-hospital community-benefit and population-health teams and self-insured employers first, then Medicare Advantage plans. The suppliers who get paid are local groups: Men's Sheds, choirs, run and walking clubs, craft circles.
problem: Social prescribing works abroad (Merton, London: GP visits down 33%, A&E visits down 50%) and WHO now attributes about 871k deaths a year to isolation. The US has no reimbursement path, so PCPs with 31-day waits have nowhere to send lonely patients. Third places run on volunteers and charity, and referral directories list them without paying them. Loneliness programs fail on retention, because people stop showing up after week 2.
solution: Screen for loneliness in primary care or at employer open enrollment (UCLA-3 or a similar short scale). The clinician sends an e-referral to a vetted local group, and the patient checks in by QR or NFC at each session. The buyer pays the group $8-15 per verified attendance, capped per member per month, and the platform keeps 15-20%. A dashboard tracks show rate at weeks 4 and 8, loneliness score change and ED or visit utilization. It is a payment and verification rail, not a social network. Groups are paid to be welcoming and to keep people coming, which is the opposite of an engagement-maximizing app.
why_now: WHO's June 2025 Commission report made loneliness a measured global health metric. Dating and social apps are stalling (Bumble layoffs, BFF relaunch), so friendship demand has no monetized supply. Medicaid work requirements from Jan 2027 and lapsed ACA subsidies are squeezing hospital margins and pushing systems toward cheap prevention with measurable ROI. Employers are also cutting expensive drug benefits and looking for low-cost wellbeing spend.
revenue_model: Per-verified-attendance settlement (buyer pays, group gets about 80-85%), plus a small PMPM or annual platform fee for the outcome dashboard and clinic workflow. Later, Medicare Advantage supplemental-benefit contracts.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing is not loneliness interventions. It is a business model for the hosts. A health payer already pays 10-100x $10 per avoided ED visit, and paying per attendance turns retention (the real failure point) into the unit of revenue. Referral directories like Findhelp route people but do not pay, and hosts cannot survive on referrals alone.
first_30_days: Recruit 15 small groups in one metro and sign each to a $10-per-attendance pilot. Sign one health-system community-benefit office or one self-insured employer for 100 referrals. Build check-in with a QR code and a spreadsheet-backed dashboard, no app needed. Measure week-4 show rate against the roughly 20-30% typical of unpaid programs, then use that number to pitch the second buyer.

title: Fractional Licensed Qualifier for Trade-Business Buyers
one_liner: Rent a vetted master-licensed professional as the bona fide qualifying officer, so first-time buyers of HVAC, plumbing, electrical and engineering firms can get financed and keep the license alive after the seller leaves.
customer: First-time acquirers (search funders, SBA-financed individual buyers, independent sponsors, small holdcos) of licensed-trade companies with $1-15M revenue. The buyer pays monthly. SBA lenders and business brokers are the referral channel.
problem: In licensed trades the license and credentials are the real asset, and they walk out the door with the seller at closing. Buyers without a license get rejected by banks, and a replacement certification takes 6-12 months. Search-fund and ETA (entrepreneurship through acquisition) volume is at record levels, so more non-credentialed buyers are chasing these businesses.
solution: A bench of retired or semi-retired license holders (master plumbers, electrical contractors, PEs, inspectors, HVAC qualifiers). Each is placed as a bona fide officer or employee under a state-specific structure with real supervisory duties, E&O cover and indemnity. The service comes with (1) a lender-ready 'credential continuity package' (letter, duties, key-person plan), (2) a 12-month program that sponsors an internal successor through exams and hours, and (3) a state-by-state compliance library. It operates only in states where counsel confirms the qualifier rules allow this. License-lending schemes are illegal in many states, so compliance is the moat.
why_now: About 100 new US/Canadian search funds launched in 2023 (record), and acquisition volume grew from $110M to $880M per Stanford data summarized on Wikipedia. More than half of US small-business owners are 55+ without succession plans. PE Hub's September 2026 feed shows continuing PE appetite for HVAC, pest control and vet add-ons, which lifts what owners of licensed businesses expect to be paid and pulls more of them into sale processes. Buyer supply now exceeds credentialed-buyer supply.
revenue_model: $2-4K/month retainer per placement for 12-24 months. $1.5-2.5K one-time lender package. Sponsored successor-certification program billed at cost plus margin. Later, group E&O and key-person insurance placement commissions.
non_obvious_insight: The binding constraint in trades acquisitions is the credential, not capital or price. Jack Rauch's Tew & Taylor deal was rejected by multiple banks because he had no building-code license or experience. Their words: 'you don't have this license, you don't have this experience... good luck. We won't touch it.' He had to close on family-office debt at a 33/33/33 cap table (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/jack-rauch-tew-taylor). Manolo Diaz Corrada's Bonneville deal names certifications as a single point of failure that take 'six months to a year to acquire' and are not economical to duplicate (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/manolo-diaz-corrada-bonneville-group). Nobody sells credential continuity as a product. Brokers treat it as the buyer's problem, and lenders treat it as a deal-killer. Caveat: the evidence is operator interviews with a small sample, and the legal structure must be validated state by state.
first_30_days: Pick two states with well-documented qualifier rules (for example FL and TX) and pay for a counsel memo on each. Recruit 10 retired license holders through trade associations, retiree groups and union alumni networks. Build a one-page lender-facing continuity plan and show it to 10-15 SBA lenders and 20 business brokers. Post the offer in ETA communities (Searchfunder, Acquiring Minds audience) and sign 2-3 buyers with signed LOIs for paid pilot placements at a discount in exchange for case studies.

title: Vet-Prescribed Walks for Post-Surgery and Senior Dogs
one_liner: Certify dog walkers to deliver vet-written controlled-walking protocols after cruciate and spinal surgery, and to send structured mobility reports back to the clinic.
customer: Owners of dogs recovering from orthopedic or spinal surgery (TPLO, luxating patella, IVDD) and owners of senior arthritic dogs. Referral partners are surgical and rehab vet practices, who get reports at no charge.
problem: Discharge sheets say things like '5-minute leash walks four times a day, add 5 minutes a week,' and working owners cannot do it. Dogs get over-exercised or under-exercised and some re-tear the repair, which is a $4k to $6k mistake. Most walkers are afraid of the liability, and most vets don't trust an unspecified walker to follow a protocol. Meanwhile arthritic seniors decline slowly and owners miss it, while the walker sees the hesitation at stairs and the shorter walks first.
solution: A short walker certification (protocol cards written with two partner rehab vets, sling and non-slip handling, escalation rules). Visits are timed, leash-controlled, and followed by a structured report covering minutes walked, a 0 to 4 gait score, stiffness on rising, toileting, and a 15-second weight-bearing video. The report goes to the owner and the clinic ahead of the 2, 6, and 8 week rechecks. Red flags (swelling, heat, toe-touching) trigger a same-day call. A senior SKU gives a monthly mobility check with a gait video and pain questionnaire, so owner and vet can see whether joint meds or the newer arthritis injectables are actually working.
why_now: Vets are short-staffed and cannot run rehab follow-ups themselves. Pet insurance adoption keeps growing, so owners protecting a multi-thousand-dollar surgery will pay for compliance. The newer arthritis injectables raised the need for objective at-home response tracking, and safety debates around them make vets want data. Return-to-office pushes more owners out of the house all day right when recoveries need multiple short visits.
revenue_model: Post-op bundle of roughly $900 to $1,800 over 6 to 8 weeks (short visits at $30 to $45), with the walker keeping about 70 percent. Walker certification fee of roughly $250 to $300. Senior monitoring subscription at about $39 a month. No referral kickbacks to vets, so it stays clean; clinics get the free reports and fewer failed recoveries.
non_obvious_insight: The most valuable clients in this business are not the healthy dogs on the schedule, they are post-op and declining dogs, because the protocol needs several short, geographically tight visits a day and the owner is desperate. The gap is trust, not supply: a protocol and a report format turn 'a walker' into a rehab extender that vets will refer to.
first_30_days: Sit down with the techs at two local surgical or rehab practices and write a one-page walking progression with them. Get yourself and three walkers through a dry run. Offer the first 10 post-op dogs a reduced bundle in exchange for report feedback, using a simple form that generates a PDF. Ask each clinic to slip a card into TPLO discharge packets and track how many convert.

title: Two-Way Kasuhara Desk for Tiny Japanese Businesses
one_liner: A QR-and-LINE 'complaint lane' plus staff backup button that gives micro-businesses the customer-harassment policy, consultation channel and evidence log Japan now requires.
customer: Owners of Japanese businesses with 1-100 employees that face customers in person (izakaya, clinics, salons, cram schools, taxi and care operators, retail). They pay ¥2,980-9,800 per site per month. Resale channels are sharoushi (labor and social-insurance consultants) and SME insurance agents.
problem: From 1 Oct 2026 every Japanese employer with at least one employee must publish a policy against customer harassment ('kasuhara'), set up and publicize a consultation channel, and have response procedures. There is no phase-in. Most tiny firms have no HR function, no policy and no channel. Staff also hesitate to report incidents. Customers, for their part, now hesitate to voice legitimate complaints.
solution: (1) A QR code at the counter, on receipts and on LINE opens a structured, polite complaint form (what happened, photo, desired resolution). The owner gets a timestamped record, and abusive or threatening messages are flagged. (2) A 'need backup' button in LINE gives frontline staff an anonymous route to a partner sharoushi or counselor. That route is the required consultation channel. (3) A one-tap incident log that creates a dated evidence pack (notes, optional call-recording notice, response taken). (4) A policy, poster and work-rule addendum generator that meets the MHLW guideline. (5) A monthly 'compliance proof' PDF for the day the labor bureau asks.
why_now: The MHLW guideline was published on 26 Feb 2026 and the duty takes effect 1 Oct 2026, three days from today. Incumbent tooling targets call centers, such as SoftBank's SoftVoice AI voice-softener launched Feb 2026. Nothing is priced or packaged for a 5-person restaurant. The Oct 1 news cycle will also push owners to search for a fix.
revenue_model: ¥2,980/month per site (¥9,800 for 10+ staff), ¥30,000 optional setup for work-rule revision, and a 30% recurring rev-share to sharoushi and insurance agents who resell it. A later upsell is per-incident counselor escalation. Insurers may white-label it into SME liability packages.
non_obvious_insight: The law has a hidden chilling effect on the customer side. In the Channel Corporation survey (497 customer-facing employees plus 514 consumers, June 2026), 52.3% of consumers who hit a store error 'let it pass' for fear of being labelled a harasser, and 65.2% wanted AI-mediated ways to raise issues. A product that gives customers a legitimate complaint lane defuses harassment at the source and doubles as the mandatory paper trail. Enforcement is guidance and then naming rather than fines, so buyers want the cheapest defensible record, not AI detection. Only under 10% of firms use technical measures. Evidence: KiteRa survey of 965 workers on 10-11 Sep 2026 found 61.3% with no policy, 68.3% with no publicized channel, 58.6% of firms with 100 or fewer employees with no channel at all, and 19.8% of workers harassed in the past year, of whom 74.9% hesitated to report (https://prtimes.jp/main/html/rd/p/000000130.000045846.html). Channel Corp found 51.7% with no measures at all (https://ecnomikata.com/ecnews/customerservice/51126/). Legal scope and enforcement: https://www.twobirds.com/en/insights/2026/singapore/customer-harassment-prevention-now-a-statutory-obligation-for-employers-in-japan. Incumbent focus on call centers: https://www.softbank.jp/en/sbnews/entry/20260219_01.
first_30_days: Days 1-3: Ship a free policy-and-poster generator plus a LINE Official Account to catch Oct 1 search traffic, and a landing page in Japanese. Days 4-14: Recruit 5-10 sharoushi (offer 30% recurring share and a white-label report) and 2 local shokokai chambers; sell 'compliance by Friday' to their existing clients. Build the QR complaint form with LINE Messaging API (no app needed) and manually route staff-backup messages to one partner counselor. Days 15-30: Sign 30-50 shops at ¥2,980 and collect 3 named case studies. Ask an SME insurance agency to pilot a bundled offer.

title: Court-Accounting Software for Family Conservators and Executors
one_liner: Statement-to-court-form automation for family members who must file annual accountings for a parent under conservatorship or through probate.
customer: Lay conservators, guardians and executors (Gen X children), plus probate attorneys, CPAs and professional fiduciaries who handle 20-200 cases.
problem: Roughly a million-plus adults are under guardianship or conservatorship, and probate cases rose about 32% from 2020 to 2024. Appointed family members must file county- and state-specific accountings with receipts and categories. Errors mean surcharges or removal, and lawyers or accountants charge $500-2,500 a filing.
solution: Connect bank accounts or upload statements, categorize against the state's court forms, flag court-sensitive items (gifts, related-party payments, unusual withdrawals), produce the accounting and receipt binder, and calendar deadlines. Include optional attorney review. Launch in California and Texas, where forms and rules are standardized.
why_now: 80+ growth means more incapacity and more estates. Elder fraud losses ($7.7B in 2025) are pushing courts to scrutinize guardians, and LLMs now parse statements accurately enough for categorization.
revenue_model: $399 a year per case for lay fiduciaries, and $79-150 per case per month for professional fiduciaries and law firms.
non_obvious_insight: Legal tech serves lawyers and estate-planning creation; nobody serves the family member who is legally required to be an amateur accountant. Court deadlines make the pain acute and the willingness to pay high.
first_30_days: Start with California and Texas. Build SEO around 'conservatorship accounting help', partner with probate attorneys, and sell the first 20 cases at $399.

title: Human Viva Examiners for AI-Wary Universities
one_liner: A per-student oral-defense service where trained examiners in Nairobi, Manila and Chennai run 12-minute recorded vivas on submitted essays and code, giving US professors human-verified authorship evidence for about $10 a student.
customer: Writing-program directors, department chairs and online-degree program managers at US community colleges and mid-size universities (intro composition, intro CS, gateway business courses). Individual adjuncts with discretionary budgets are the first buyers. Admissions offices reviewing flagged essays come second.
problem: Harvard data from Sept 2026: 89% of professors received suspected AI work, 67% say AI hurts their courses, and only 12% referred cases to the honor council. Detectors are unreliable and biased against non-native writers. Nobody has the time or the standing to test an accusation, and a professor cannot personally hold 60 oral exams per section.
solution: The instructor uploads submissions and a rubric. The platform drafts 4-6 questions specific to each student's own paper. AI writes the questions but never judges. A vetted examiner in a matching time zone runs a 12-minute live video viva, scores it against the rubric, and marks the student as able or unable to explain their own work. The instructor gets a one-page evidence summary and the recording within 48 hours. Examiners are ex-teachers and graduate students who pass a 6-hour certification, and 10% of vivas are double-scored for QA. Students consent through the syllabus, and the institution signs a FERPA school-official agreement.
why_now: Faculty AI distress peaked in Sept 2026. NYC and LAUSD paused classroom AI for 2026-27, so 'human-verified' is now politically favored over AI-judging-AI. Proctored math accuracy has fallen from about 80% to about 60% while unsupervised work looks better. Meanwhile English-fluent graduates in Kenya, the Philippines and India face a shrinking entry-level BPO ladder, so a large trainable labor pool is available at $15/hour.
revenue_model: $9-14 per viva billed to the department, with examiners paid about $4-5 per viva (roughly $15/hour), for a gross margin near 55%. Departments can buy an annual site licence of $3-10k. An appeal viva is a $25 add-on.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not detection, it is credible human attention. Detectors create accusations nobody can test, while a viva turns an accusation into an assessment: if the student can defend the paper, they learned it, however they drafted it. The only way to supply cheap, trusted, trained human minutes at scale is emerging-market labor, and the only buyers who will pay are institutions that just lost faith in remote work.
first_30_days: Recruit and train 15 examiners through two teacher-training colleges or alumni groups in Kenya and the Philippines. Offer three community-college composition instructors a free 30-student pilot and record what share of students cannot explain their own paper. Charge $300 for the next batch, and reach instructors through adjunct communities and online-program managers. Run it on Zoom, a calendar tool and Airtable, with no custom platform until 10 paying sections exist.

title: Origin Assay: Forensic Testing of Metal Melt Origin
one_liner: A lab test that says where steel or aluminum was actually melted, so US-melt claims stop resting on paperwork alone.
customer: Importers and fabricators claiming the 10% US-melt rate, steel service centers selling premium 'US-melt' stock, customs counsel and insurers defending CBP audits, and buyers with domestic-metal requirements.
problem: Section 232 rates now depend on melt or smelt origin: 10% with US-melted metal against 25-50%. The certificate is worth thousands of dollars per ton, mill test reports can be relabeled or forged, and CBP is prioritizing origin verification and AD/CVD evasion. No independent test exists.
solution: Build a reference library by buying coupons from about 100 mills worldwide. Measure trace-element, inclusion and slag chemistry, and isotopic signatures (LIBS, ICP-MS, SEM-EDS). Train a classifier to give origin probability. First product is a mail-in Origin Assay with a confidence-scored report and sampling protocol built for audits. Handheld screening is a later roadmap. Classifier accuracy is the central risk, so start with one narrow discrimination, such as US EAF versus Chinese plate for one grade.
why_now: The 2026 tiers turn a chemistry fact into a financial asset. Cheaper mass spectrometry and machine learning make library-based classification plausible, and academic provenance work exists but no commercial library does (verify).
revenue_model: $300-900 per sample. $25-100k annual audit programs for service centers. Insurer verification programs. Later, handheld subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Duty policy turned melt origin into money, and paper certificates invite cheating, so the arbitrage is proof. Scrap-based EAF steel carries a fingerprint of tramp elements and alloy history that makes origin partly knowable.
first_30_days: Interview three service centers and three customs counsel. Buy or borrow about 40 heats of known origin (A36 and 304). Use a university ICP-MS lab to test discriminating power on two grades. Sell a $5k pilot verification of 10 suspicious heats.

title: Guard-Shack Handshake: Stopping Fictitious Pickups at the Gate
one_liner: A free, no-login gate tool for shipper guard shacks that shows the pre-enrolled driver, truck, plate and a one-time PIN, paid for per protected load by brokers and cargo insurers.
customer: Brokers moving high-theft commodities (electronics, copper and other metals, consumer goods, food and beverage) and their cargo and contingent-cargo insurers pay. Shippers get the guard tool free, which is what drives adoption.
problem: CargoNet estimates H1 2026 cargo theft losses above $359M, with Q2 2026 losses of $304.6M (more than double Q2 2025) even though incidents fell, driven by high-value metals and technology. Criminals now compromise legitimate carrier accounts, internet-based phone systems, email and compliance-platform credentials, so the email domain, callback number and vetting badge can all be authentic-looking. Meanwhile at the physical gate a guard checks a load number and a BOL, as in 1995. The load number is a password that the broker has already emailed to dozens of carriers.
solution: At tender, the broker's rate-con flow triggers a driver self-enrollment via SMS link: selfie, CDL photo, truck and trailer plate photos. The system checks how recently the carrier's public contact info changed and whether the enrolling number matches prior loads. The shipper's shipping desk and guard get a web link (no app, no integration) showing the expected driver photo, plate and USDOT number. The driver must speak a PIN issued only through the enrollment. The guard taps match or mismatch and snaps an arrival photo, and any mismatch alerts the broker and shipper instantly. The receiver gets the same flow at delivery. Aggregated data goes to insurers.
why_now: The 2026 CargoNet reports describe impersonation-based theft as systematic and scalable, with credential and phone-system compromise defeating digital-only checks. Montgomery (May 2026) raised broker liability, and insurers are now asking brokers for controls. The Jan 2026 FMCSA rule means a broker who pays a big theft claim can drop below the bond threshold and face suspension.
revenue_model: $2-$5 per protected load charged to brokers, plus an insurer revenue share or bounty for verified low-loss books. Later, sell a 'verified pickup' certificate to cargo insurers in exchange for lower deductibles.
non_obvious_insight: The thief needs two things, a load number and a plausible carrier identity, and the broker hands out both freely. Nobody has redesigned the 30-second guard-shack transaction because shippers feel the cargo is no longer theirs once the BOL is signed, so the party that eats the loss (broker or insurer) has to fund a free tool for the party that controls the gate. The best fraud tell is not the carrier's score but the age of its contact info: hijacked carriers show new phones and emails days before booking. Brokers whisper this in fraud groups but no product sells it.
first_30_days: Sign 3 brokers hauling metals or electronics and pick 5 recurring shipper docks. Build a web-only MVP (SMS enrollment plus guard view) and run the PINs manually. Pilot 100 loads, measuring driver friction (target under 90 seconds) and catch rate with seeded red-team tests. Get one cargo insurer or MGA to review the pilot data for a premium credit.

title: Forensic Chat-Log Analysis for AI-Harm Lawsuits
one_liner: A court-defensible method and service that turns exported chatbot transcripts into escalation timelines, sycophancy evidence and missed-crisis reports for plaintiffs, defense counsel and regulators.
customer: Plaintiff firms handling AI wrongful-death and psychosis cases, defense counsel at AI companies and app makers, and state attorneys general, paying $10-30k per case plus expert-witness fees.
problem: Trend chain: over a million weekly suicide-related conversations with general chatbots (OpenAI, Oct 2025), then Raine v. OpenAI plus at least nine similar suits, then hundreds of thousands of words of transcript per case with no standard way to measure sycophancy, delusion reinforcement or whether crisis protocols fired. Expert testimony is ad hoc, and the first Daubert-style challenges are coming.
solution: A clinician-designed coding manual plus a software pipeline. It ingests exports from ChatGPT, Character.ai and Replika formats and tags each turn for risk disclosure, model response type (refuse, validate, encourage, refer) and escalation, then produces an evidentiary report with reproducibility statistics and inter-rater reliability from two clinician coders plus model assistance.
why_now: The litigation wave is live, Pennsylvania's Department of State sued in May 2026, the Human Line Project reports members in 22 countries with logs in hand, and no accepted methodology exists yet. Whoever's method survives the first challenge becomes the standard.
revenue_model: Per-case fixed fee of $10-30k, subscriptions for firms with multiple cases, expert-witness and training fees, later insurer and state-AG contracts.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not AI. It is a validated, adversarially tested coding scheme that survives its first Daubert challenge, like DNA or forensic accounting. Because defense will need the same method, the business is side-agnostic and cannot be undercut by a lab.
first_30_days: Recruit a forensic psychiatrist and a forensic linguist. Code the excerpts quoted in five public complaints to build a v0.1 manual. Offer three plaintiff firms a free two-week pilot analysis on one case each, then convert to fixed fees and publish a methods note.

title: Contest-Proof Signing: Capacity Sessions for Wills
one_liner: A recorded, clinician-run capacity and intent session at will signing, so a later contest by disappointed heirs has strong evidence against it.
customer: Estate-planning and elder-law attorneys and RIAs whose clients are 75+, in blended families or making unequal bequests. Clients pay the clinical entity directly, and firms bundle it into fixed-fee packages.
problem: An older wealthy cohort, more second marriages and rising dementia diagnoses mean more disputes about capacity and undue influence. Evidence of capacity at signing is usually the drafting lawyer's memory plus boilerplate. That is weak in court and expensive to defend.
solution: A standardized signing-day product. A licensed geriatric psychiatrist or neuropsychologist runs a structured, recorded interview with validated screening, an independent private conversation without family, and a recorded 'why I chose this' statement. The bundle is hashed and stored under the attorney's privilege, with an optional yearly refresh and in-home or remote delivery.
why_now: FDA cleared blood tests for Alzheimer's pathology in 2025, so more people get an early diagnosis and want to sign while they still can. Remote notarization and e-will laws widened access, and video is cheap. The transfer is concentrated in older households with complex families.
revenue_model: $700-$1,500 per session billed by the clinical entity, firm-level packages of $25K/year, and yearly refresh sessions. Lawyer referral-fee rules make direct client billing the safer structure (check state ethics rules).
non_obvious_insight: Capacity is a moment-in-time question and the evidence is manufactured at the signing. It is cheap to create then and impossible to recreate later. Diagnosis awareness is creating a rush window nobody is serving.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 geriatric psychiatrists or neuropsychologists per metro. Partner with 5 elder-law firms. Run 20 sessions at $900 and have each firm's litigators review the artifact bundle. Keep clean records of what each session found.

title: Book-Not-Shop Roll-Up of Retiring Machine Shops
one_liner: Buy retiring shops' customer books, programs and drawings on earn-outs, then migrate the work to a partner network.
customer: Owners of 5-40 person machine shops aged 60+ who want a clean exit. The buyer's customers keep their supply.
problem: About 60% of US manufacturing firms have owners aged 55+, about 150k small and mid-size firms are near retirement, and customers often leave when the owner retires (per American Machinist and MMS). MMS admits no dataset exists. Existing buyers such as Compass Precision buy whole shops with real estate, iron and payroll, which is capital-heavy and risky.
solution: Buy only the customer relationships, drawings, programs, fixtures and quality records for about 1-1.5x annual gross profit, paid mostly as an earn-out on retained revenue over 24-36 months. The owner runs a transition site for 6-12 months. Work then moves to 3-5 partner shops that have spare capacity. Equipment is auctioned or leased. AI digitizes quote history and setup sheets.
why_now: The retirement wave is under way and PMI at 55.6 (highest since May 2022) keeps demand steady. PE roll-ups have proven that a market exists, and a capital-light structure fits smaller teams.
revenue_model: 15-25% gross margin on migrated work. Slotting fees from partner shops. Deal capital is $250-750k per deal, mostly as earn-out.
non_obvious_insight: The asset is customer trust and tacit programs, not buildings or machines. An earn-out tied to retained revenue makes both sides fight the main failure mode of roll-ups, which is customer attrition.
first_30_days: Build a list of 300 target shops from state registries, LinkedIn and outreach. Sign three LOIs on owner-friendly terms. Line up three partner shops with capacity. Raise a $1M search-fund-style pool or use SBA financing.

title: Notary Network for Human-Verified Hiring
one_liner: Bonded local human witnesses (mostly mobile notaries and loan-signing agents) sit with a job candidate for a phone-free live work sample and sign an attestation the employer can rely on.
customer: Remote-first companies of 20-2,000 people hiring for roles that touch code, money, patient data or production systems (fintech, health-tech, cybersecurity, engineering, back-office BPO), plus staffing and recruiting agencies placing remote workers. The first buyer is a 30-person startup that cannot fly candidates to HQ.
problem: Video interviews are no longer trustworthy evidence of who is doing the work. Real-time face-swaps, proxy test-takers and AI feeding answers are common: a 2026 Greenhouse survey reportedly found 91% of US hiring managers had encountered or suspected AI-generated answers, and Gartner projects that by 2028 one in four candidate profiles will be synthetic. Google and McKinsey reportedly reintroduced in-person verification steps, but a small remote employer cannot fly every finalist in, and detection software is an arms race the defenders keep losing.
solution: A marketplace of vetted, insured, background-checked local witnesses. The candidate meets one at a library room or coworking space. The witness checks government ID in person, hands the candidate a locked-down laptop or a paper packet, and stays through a 60-90 minute live work sample or technical interview run by the employer over the employer's own video call. No phones are allowed in the room. The witness signs a notarial-style attestation (ID match, unbroken presence, session log, photo) that goes into the employer's applicant file. Sold as a $150-250 per-session add-on to the final-round interview. The same primitive later extends to bootcamp and university oral exams, licensing bodies, and witnessed authorship for authors and artists.
why_now: In 2026, deepfake candidates are ranked among the top fraud threats by Experian, and hiring teams are openly adding in-person checks. Meanwhile mortgage volume is still well below its 2021 peak, so tens of thousands of trained loan-signing agents have idle capacity and already know how to verify identity and witness a signature. Remote notarization and gig onboarding tools make a distributed 1099 witness network cheap to stand up.
revenue_model: Employers pay $150-250 per attested session (witness keeps roughly 55%). Subscription tiers for volume hirers ($500-2,000 per month with session credits). Enterprise and staffing-agency contracts with bulk pricing. Later: per-exam fees from education and credentialing bodies.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not better deepfake detection but a cheap, trusted, physical human at a known place, and the law already has an institution for that: the notary. A loan-signing workforce is already trained, insured and idle. The purchase also gets filed under fraud and insider-risk compliance (nation-state fake-IT-worker schemes, SOC 2 evidence) rather than HR, which means bigger budgets and faster approval.
first_30_days: Recruit 30 signing agents in three metros through notary Facebook groups and NotaryCafe-type forums, with a simple 1099 onboarding. Write the session protocol and attestation PDF in a week; run booking and payment with Airtable and Stripe. Cold-email 100 remote-heavy startups and staffing firms with the offer 'we will send a human to sit with your finalist, first 3 sessions at $99'. Aim for 10 paid sessions by day 30. Publish an anonymized case study of the first mismatch or coached-answer catch.

title: Posthumous Likeness Trusts for Creators
one_liner: Estate planning for people whose face and voice already earn money: who may license their AI replica, who may not, and how it is enforced.
customer: Mid-tier creators (100K-5M followers), podcasters, voice actors, and the small managers and MCNs who represent them.
problem: Consumer-grade video and voice cloning means anyone's likeness can be recreated after death. Laws are a patchwork (Tennessee's ELVIS Act and California's 2024 digital-replica laws, a federal NO FAKES bill pending). Creators' estates hold real income (channels, catalogs, sponsorships) but have no instrument to permit, forbid or license replicas. Platforms handle it ad hoc.
solution: A 'Likeness Trust Kit': (1) a will or trust addendum with a digital-replica directive (allowed uses, revenue splits, ban list, who decides), (2) a registry and notice system aimed at platforms and AI vendors, (3) monitoring for unauthorized replicas and template takedowns, (4) a channel-continuity plan (access, memorialization, pinned messages), and (5) an optional licensing desk for approved 'legacy' uses.
why_now: The fall-2025 backlash over AI videos of deceased public figures made estates' concerns public. State post-mortem publicity laws changed in 2024, and platforms have begun shipping likeness-detection tools for creators (verify current status). No estate product has priced in that a voice and face are now licensable and misusable assets.
revenue_model: $1,500-$3,500 setup for documents and registry, $19-$79/month monitoring, and 10-20% of licensed uses. Managers buy in bulk.
non_obvious_insight: Estate lawyers treat likeness as a celebrity issue. The willing buyers are working creators who already understand platforms and already earn from their persona, and they are numerous and reachable through managers.
first_30_days: Partner with an entertainment attorney. Draft a template addendum. Sell to 10 creator managers at about $2K per client. Use off-the-shelf detection tools for monitoring and publish a public 'creator death checklist' for lead generation.

title: Battery EPR Desk for E-Mobility Importers
one_liner: A retainer compliance service that registers, reports and budgets for battery EPR on behalf of small e-bike, scooter and power-station brands.
customer: E-bike, e-scooter, power-station and power-tool brand owners and importers of record selling into California and other battery-EPR states, typically $2-100M revenue with no regulatory staff.
problem: California signed SB 501 on Sept 20, 2026, creating medium-format battery EPR with a 60% recycling-efficiency floor. Thousands of small importers and marketplace sellers cannot parse who counts as the producer, how to pick or join a PRO, or what to report. Their packs also drive facility fires.
solution: Producer determination, PRO registration, automated unit and weight reporting from Shopify and Amazon data, fee budgeting, labeling artwork, take-back partnering, and a battery data sheet (chemistry, mass, removability). Recyclers want that sheet, and the evidence pack satisfies audits.
why_now: SB 501 was signed days ago, and California signed it while vetoing other bills. Existing state battery laws and the 74 catastrophic facility fires this year mean regulators and marketplaces will demand proof.
revenue_model: $6-24K per year retainer, plus 5-10% markup on pass-through PRO fees and take-back costs.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is not the famous brand but 3,000 small importers who cannot read statute. Becoming the compliance layer that marketplaces reference flips the distribution problem.
first_30_days: Build an 'Am I a producer?' quiz. Scrape marketplaces for e-mobility brands selling into California and email 300. Sign 10 for a $1.5K registration audit. Approach one marketplace's compliance team.

title: Contingency Collection for Small-Claims Winners
one_liner: Post-judgment enforcement for the $500-$10k creditor who won in court but cannot collect: skip-trace, levy and garnishment paperwork done for a percentage.
customer: Small landlords with unpaid-rent or damage judgments, tenants with deposit judgments, freelancers and contractor-fraud victims, paying a $99 setup plus 25-30% of dollars actually recovered.
problem: Roughly 70-80% of civil and small-claims judgments go uncollected, and the winner must find assets and file every enforcement step alone. Enforcement costs can exceed the judgment, tenants disappear without forwarding addresses, and attorneys skip small cases. Cheap filing tools like trysmallclaims ($149 demand letter, $299 filing) stop at judgment.
solution: Automate post-judgment work: skip-trace the debtor, discover employer and bank via debtor-exam forms, e-file state-specific wage garnishment and bank levy packets, schedule sheriff or constable levies, and calendar renewals and follow-ups. A partner licensed collection agency or attorney in each state handles regulatory compliance. Offer a pre-filing 'collectability score' so creditors learn whether the defendant has a job or bank account before spending on court.
why_now: Self-serve filing tools are creating more small-claims judgments, while enforcement remains manual and state-specific. Consumer data APIs and LLM document drafting make per-state packets cheap, and small landlords face rising unpaid-rent losses and slow evictions, so many are holding judgments they cannot collect.
revenue_model: 25-30% contingency on recovered dollars, $99 setup fee, and a $19 collectability score for pre-filing triage; later B2B seats for landlord associations and property managers.
non_obvious_insight: A widely cited split says about 20% of debtors pay voluntarily, 60% are 'strategic avoiders' who have assets but make the creditor work, and 20% are judgment-proof (https://www.trysmallclaims.com/blog/small-claims-court-judgment-enforcement-tools-by-state). The middle 60% is a repeatable, automatable playbook, and the competitor sells only filing and demand letters. The ABA Journal notes about 80% of civil money judgments remain unenforced and that only 3 of the top 50 law schools teach judgment enforcement (https://www.abajournal.com/voice/article/why-do-80-of-judgments-remain-uncollected). Landlord-side friction is described at https://www.fastevictionservice.com/blog/why-small-claims-court-judgments-are-hard-to-enforce/, which notes costs 'sometimes exceeding the amount of the judgment itself'. Reddit was unreachable, so the r/Landlord and r/legaladvice 'I won, now how do I collect?' pattern is inferred from these secondary sources.
first_30_days: Pick California or Texas. Approach two local apartment or landlord associations and collect 10-20 existing unpaid judgments on contingency. Sign a licensed collection agency or attorney partner, build the skip-trace plus writ and levy templates for one county, run garnishments manually first, and publish recovery statistics after the first 5 collections.

title: Drone-Checked Eruv Boundaries
one_liner: Scheduled autonomous drone inspection of the utility-wire boundaries that define an eruv, so communities learn before Shabbat whether a line is down.
customer: Eruv committees and synagogues in the US and abroad (hundreds of communities), plus Jewish federations and city-level committees.
problem: An eruv's boundary is often miles of utility wire, checked weekly by volunteers on foot or by car. A break invalidates carrying on Shabbat, and storms and tree limbs cause breaks. Utilities do not notify committees.
solution: Weekly autonomous flights (drone-in-a-box under Part 107 first, then BVLOS), computer-vision detection of wire discontinuity and pole damage, and GPS-pinned photo alerts to the committee. The rabbinic authority stays the decision-maker, and the tool provides the time-stamped evidence.
why_now: The FAA's Part 108 BVLOS rule cleared to OIRA (final review) in July 2026 and was not yet published as of mid-September. Drone docks and vision models are cheap. A 2016 proposal in Israel showed interest but no commercial product surfaced.
revenue_model: $300-1,500/month per eruv plus a setup fee, then adjacent inspection contracts (cemetery and campus perimeters, congregation roofs and steeples).
non_obvious_insight: The religious need is verification, not construction. A weekly audit trail with time-stamped imagery is exactly what a committee needs for its Friday declaration, which converts a religious-legal requirement into a recurring inspection budget line.
first_30_days: Contact 5 eruv committees (for example Baltimore, Teaneck, Cleveland). Fly VLOS segments with a Part 107 pilot, build a wire-break detection dataset, and sign 2 paid pilots at about $250/month.
